mainTopic: The Persian lamp story, רבי אמי's two reports of רבי יוחנן on who may deliver a split-testimony גט, a new משנה on writing and signing by day or night, and why a גט must be dated.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a story. A Persian priest takes away the sages' lamp, and רבה בר בר חנה cries out that he would rather live under Rome than under the Persians. The גמרא asks how that fits with רבי חייא, who taught that God sent the Jews to Babylonia because Roman rule was too hard for them. It answers that רבי חייא spoke of the time before the Persians came to Babylonia, and רבה בר בר חנה spoke of the time after. Then the גמרא returns to the משנה's case of one witness to the writing and two to the signing. רבי אמי, quoting רבי יוחנן, first says this works only when the writing witness delivers the גט. Later he rules that even the signing witnesses may deliver it. When רבי אסי points out the contradiction, רבי אמי calls his second ruling "a peg that will not move." A new משנה follows about a גט written by day or by night, and רבי שמעון explains why he accepts a גט signed the night after it was written. The גמרא then asks why a גט needs a date at all. רבי יוחנן says it is because of a man married to his niece, and ריש לקיש says it is because of the produce of the wife's fields. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to explain why ריש לקיש did not accept רבי יוחנן's reason, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Persian priest takes the lamp, and a cry for Roman rule
steps.stepSummary: A Persian priest takes the lamp away from the sages. רבה בר בר חנה cries out that he would rather live under God's protection or under Rome than under Persia.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Persian priest came and took the lamp from in front of them. He said: Merciful One! Either in Your shadow, or in the shadow of the son of Esau.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story: while the sages were visiting the sick רבה בר בר חנה, a Persian priest took away their lamp. Upset, רבה בר בר חנה prayed to be under God's protection, or at least under Rome rather than Persia.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Persians had a holiday when ordinary people were not allowed to keep a light outside their temple, so the priest took the lamp. רבה בר בר חנה came from ארץ ישראל, which was under Roman rule. He felt Roman rule was easier than this Persian harshness. This sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.english: A Persian priest took the lamp from before them.
He said: Merciful One!
Either in Your shadow,
or in the shadow of the son of Esau.
phrases.notes: "Son of Esau" means the Romans. He would rather live under Rome than under the Persians.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: רַחֲמָנָא! אוֹ בְּטוּלָּךְ, אוֹ בְּטוּלָּא דְּבַר עֵשָׂו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a story that began before this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה בר בר חנה expresses that Roman rule is better than Persian rule.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי חייא says Babylonia is better than Rome
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how Rome could be better, when רבי חייא taught that God sent the Jews to Babylonia because they could not bear Roman decrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean the Romans are better than the Persians? But רבי חייא taught: What does the פסוק mean, "God understands its way and He knows its place"? הקדוש ברוך הוא knows that the Jewish people cannot accept Roman decrees, so He exiled them to Babylonia.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה בר בר חנה's prayer. It quotes רבי חייא, who said God sent the Jews to Babylonia because Roman rule would be too hard for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה's words suggest Rome is easier to live under than Babylonia. רבי חייא says the opposite: God chose Babylonia for the exile because it is gentler than Rome. Both cannot be true as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? (opens a challenge to an implication)

phrases.english: Is this to say that the Romans are better than the Persians?!
But didn't רבי חייא teach:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"God understands its way
and He knows its place"?
The Holy One, Blessed be He, knows about the Jewish people
that they are not able to bear the decrees of the Romans,
so He arose and exiled them to Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרוֹמָאֵי מְעַלּוּ מִפָּרְסָאֵי? וְהָתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what רבה בר בר חנה's prayer implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea from step 1 that Roman rule is better than rule in Babylonia.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא's teaching says God picked Babylonia because it is easier than Rome. That contradicts the claim that Rome is better.

steps.title: Answer: Before and after the Persians came to Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: The two statements describe different times. רבי חייא speaks of Babylonia before the Persians arrived. רבה בר בר חנה speaks of after they arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This (רבי חייא) was before the Persians came to Babylonia. That (רבה בר בר חנה) was after the Persians came to Babylonia.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each statement fits a different period in history.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the Persians took over, Babylonia really was the gentler place, as רבי חייא taught. After the Persians arrived, life there became harsh, so רבה בר בר חנה preferred Rome. Both statements are true, each for its own time.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
This one... that one... (splits two cases apart)
The Persians (the Persian priests and their rule)

steps.whatToRemember: Babylonia was better than Rome only before the Persians came. After they came, Rome seemed better.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this was before the Persians came to Babylonia,
phrases.notes: "This" is רבי חייא's teaching about the exile.

phrases.english: that was after the Persians came to Babylonia.
phrases.notes: "That" is רבה בר בר חנה's prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; הָא מִקַּמֵּי דְּנֵיתוֹ חַבָּרֵי לְבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by time period (two different realities)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought both statements spoke about the same time and so contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חייא describes Babylonia before the Persian takeover. רבה בר בר חנה describes it after.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: one witness to the writing, two to the signing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: if one person says the גט was written before him and two say it was signed before them, the גט is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one says, "It was written in my presence," and two say, "It was signed in our presence," it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its case to set up the next discussion. This line is a setup for רבי יוחנן's teaching that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone bringing a גט from overseas normally has to say "בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם". In this case, the testimony is split. One person speaks about the writing, and two others speak about the signing. The משנה says this is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: It was written in my presence
It was signed in our presence

phrases.english: One says: "It was written in my presence,"
and two say: "It was signed in our presence,"
it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר בְּפָנַי נִכְתַּב וּשְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים בְּפָנֵינוּ נֶחְתַּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the משנה to begin a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט is valid when one person testifies about the writing and two testify about the signing.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: valid only if the writing witness delivers the גט
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי quotes רבי יוחנן: the משנה is valid only when the person who saw the writing is the one delivering the גט. If the signing witnesses deliver it, it is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They only taught this when the גט comes out from the hand of the witness to the writing. Then they become like two on this and two on that. But if it comes from the hands of the signing witnesses, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן limits the משנה's case. It works only if the one who saw the גט written is also the messenger who hands it over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The messenger is trusted like two witnesses. So when he testifies about the writing, the writing has the strength of two witnesses, and the signing already has two. If the signing witnesses bring the גט instead, the writing has only one ordinary witness behind it. That is not enough, so the גט is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when... (limits a teaching)
Comes out from the hand of (is delivered by)
The witness who saw the writing

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's split testimony works only when the writing witness is the messenger. He counts like two, so both the writing and the signing have two witnesses.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think "two on this and two on that" means four separate people. The single messenger counts like two for the writing.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the messenger of a גט has special trust, as strong as two witnesses. That trust is what makes this split testimony work.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רבי אמי said that רבי יוחנן said:
They only taught this

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהַגֵּט יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יַד עֵד כְּתִיבָה,
phrases.english: when the גט is delivered by the witness to the writing,
since they become like two for this
and like two for that;
but if it is delivered by the signing witnesses
it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the case of the משנה quoted in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The split testimony is valid only when the writing witness delivers the גט. If the signing witnesses deliver it, the גט is invalid.

steps.title: What follows from רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that, according to רבי יוחנן, two people who bring a גט from overseas must declare that it was both written and signed in their presence.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems רבי יוחנן holds that two people who brought a גט from overseas must say: 'It was written before us and it was signed before us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out what רבי יוחנן's ruling in Step 5 must be based on. This sets up רבי אסי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, the גט was invalid when the signing witnesses delivered it. The only good reason is that delivering pairs must testify to both the writing and the signing. The signing witnesses can only say 'signed before us,' so the גט fails.

keyTerms.meaning: So it seems / evidently: introduces a conclusion drawn from what was just said
A country overseas, outside ארץ ישראל
It was written before us and it was signed before us: the required declaration

phrases.english: Apparently he holds:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יוחנן, whose ruling רבי אמי just quoted.

phrases.english: Two who brought a bill of divorce from overseas
are required to say:
'It was written before us and it was signed before us.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the underlying principle behind רבי יוחנן's ruling in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people who bring a גט from overseas must declare both the writing and the signing in their presence.

steps.title: Does the first clause invalidate even when both deliver?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי asks: if so, then in the משנה's first clause the חכמים would invalidate the גט even when both of them deliver it. Is that really so?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said to him: If that is so, look at the first clause, which teaches: if two say 'it was written before us' and one says 'it was signed before me,' it is invalid, and רבי יהודה says it is valid. Would the חכמים invalidate it even when the גט is delivered by both of them?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי tests the new rule against the first clause of the משנה. The rule seems to give a surprising result there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause, only one person testifies to the signing. Under the rule from Step 6, the two deliverers cannot say 'signed before us.' So the חכמים would have to invalidate the גט even if the two deliver it together, and רבי אסי finds that hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: introduces a hard consequence of what was just said
Comes out from the hands of, meaning delivered by

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said to him,
But if so, the first clause which teaches:
Two say 'it was written before us'
and one says 'it was signed before me': invalid,
and Rabbi Yehuda declares it valid;

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ גֵּט יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יְדֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם –
phrases.english: and even when the bill of divorce is delivered by both of them,
do the Rabbis invalidate it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי, אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, רֵישָׁא דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of Step 6 by applying it to the משנה's first clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that two deliverers must declare both writing and signing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that rule, the חכמים in the first clause would invalidate the גט even when both deliver it, which seems too extreme.

steps.title: רבי אמי accepts: yes, it is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that yes, the חכמים invalidate it even then.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי simply accepts the result of רבי אסי's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not look for a way around the question. He agrees that in the first clause the גט is invalid even when both deliver it, because the deliverers cannot say 'signed before us.'

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 7 by accepting its conclusion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed too extreme that the חכמים would invalidate even when both deliver.
steps.terutzMaskana: Yes, under this view the חכמים do invalidate in that case.

steps.title: Another time: delivered by the signing witnesses is valid
steps.stepSummary: Another time, רבי אסי found רבי אמי teaching that even a גט delivered by the signing witnesses is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time, he found him sitting and saying that even if the גט is delivered by the signing witnesses, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of a different occasion when רבי אמי taught the opposite of Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, a גט delivered by the signing witnesses was invalid. Now רבי אמי says it is valid. This is a direct reversal.

keyTerms.meaning: The witnesses who signed the document

phrases.english: Another time he found him sitting and saying,
phrases.notes: רבי אסי found רבי אמי teaching.

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲפִילּוּ גֵּט יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יְדֵי עֵדֵי חֲתִימָה – כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: that even if the bill of divorce is delivered by the signing witnesses, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִימְנִין אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ דְּיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a second ruling from רבי אמי that reverses Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט delivered by the signing witnesses is valid.

steps.title: What follows from the second ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that, by this ruling, two people who bring a גט from overseas do not need to say 'written before us and signed before us.'
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems he holds that two people who brought a גט from overseas do not need to say: 'It was written before us and it was signed before us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out the principle behind the new ruling. This sets up רבי אסי's next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the signing witnesses can deliver the גט even though they cannot say 'written before us,' then a pair of deliverers does not need the full declaration. This is the exact opposite of the inference in Step 6.

phrases.english: Apparently he holds:
Two who brought a bill of divorce from overseas
are not required to say:
'It was written before us and it was signed before us.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the principle behind the second ruling in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people who bring a גט from overseas do not need the full declaration.

steps.title: Then the first clause would be valid if both deliver?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי reads the first clause again. It is invalid only because the two did not deliver it together, so if they did, the חכמים would say it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said to him: If so, look at the first clause: if two say 'it was written before us' and one says 'it was signed before me,' it is invalid, and רבי יהודה says it is valid. The reason it is invalid is that the גט is not delivered by both of them. But if the גט is delivered by both of them, would the חכמים say it is valid?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי checks how the new principle fits the first clause of the משנה. He asks רבי אמי to confirm what it implies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the new view, the deliverers do not need the full declaration. So in the first clause, the only problem must be that the גט was not delivered by both of them. That implies the חכמים would accept it if both delivered it, which is the opposite of what רבי אמי said in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: But then: introduces what follows by implication

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said to him:
But if so, the first clause which teaches:
Two say 'it was written before us'
and one says 'it was signed before me': invalid,
and Rabbi Yehuda declares it valid;

phrases.aramaic: טַעְמָא דְּאֵין הַגֵּט יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יְדֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם,
phrases.english: the reason is that the bill of divorce is not delivered by both of them,

phrases.aramaic: הָא גֵּט יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יְדֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם –
phrases.english: but if the bill of divorce is delivered by both of them,
do the Rabbis declare it valid?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, רֵישָׁא דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the new principle of Step 10 to the משנה's first clause, mirroring Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, under the new view, the חכמים would declare the גט valid if both of them delivered it.

steps.title: רבי אמי confirms: yes, valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that yes, the חכמים would declare it valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי confirms what רבי אסי drew from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This 'yes' is the opposite of the 'yes' in Step 8. There, the חכמים invalidated even when both delivered. Here, they would declare it valid.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the implication raised in Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the חכמים would declare it valid when both deliver it.

steps.title: But you once taught us the opposite
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי points out that on the earlier occasion רבי אמי did not say this.
steps.simpleTranslation: But on the other occasion you did not tell us this!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי challenges רבי אמי by setting his two answers side by side, since they clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Steps 5 to 8, רבי אמי ruled that the signing witnesses cannot deliver the גט, and that the first clause is invalid even when both deliver. Now he says the reverse on both points. Both cannot be רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: You did not tell us this

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא זִמְנִין לָא אֲמַרְתְּ לַן הָכִי!
phrases.english: But the other time you did not tell us so!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא זִמְנִין לָא אֲמַרְתְּ לַן הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the ruling just confirmed in Step 12 against the earlier ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's two conflicting reports of רבי יוחנן's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same teacher gave opposite rulings on the same case, so one of them must be wrong.

steps.title: A peg that will not move: the final ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי declares that his present ruling is firm and reliable. He drops the earlier one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is a peg that will not move.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי settles the contradiction by declaring the second ruling final.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not try to reconcile the two rulings. He pulls back from the first one and fixes the second as firm. So a גט delivered by the signing witnesses is valid, and two deliverers do not need the full declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: A peg or tent stake: an image of something firmly fixed
That will not move or shake

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי's final word for רבי יוחנן: a גט delivered by the signing witnesses is valid. Two who bring a גט from overseas do not need to say 'written before us and signed before us.' The earlier, stricter ruling is withdrawn.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two 'yes' answers. The first (Step 8) belongs to the ruling that was dropped. The second (Step 12) is the one that stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an אמורא can openly take back an earlier teaching, and it fixes which version of רבי יוחנן's view the סוגיא relies on.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יָתֵד הִיא שֶׁלֹּא תָּמוּט.
phrases.english: He said to him: It is a peg that will not move.
phrases.notes: He means: 'This ruling is fixed; rely on it, not on what I said before.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יָתֵד הִיא שֶׁלֹּא תָּמוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction of Step 13 by withdrawing the earlier ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: one ruling is declared final and the other withdrawn
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings seemed to be רבי יוחנן's view, which is contradictory.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second ruling, that the signing witnesses may deliver the גט, is the firm one.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A גט delivered by the signing witnesses is valid, and two deliverers do not need the full declaration.

steps.title: New משנה: Writing and signing a גט by day or by night
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists four timing cases. Three are כשר and one is פסול, but רבי שמעון rules that one כשר too.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גט written by day and signed that day is valid. One written at night and signed that night is valid. One written at night and signed the next day is valid. One written by day and signed that night is invalid, but רבי שמעון says it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It rules on whether a גט is valid when the writing and the signing happen at different times of day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In הלכה, a new day begins at nightfall. So night followed by the next day is still one date, but day followed by that night crosses into a new date. When that happens, the date written in the גט is earlier than the day it was signed. The חכמים say that makes it פסול, while רבי שמעון disagrees.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think in terms of a day that starts in the morning. The night comes before its day, so 'night, then the next day' is the same date.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: If it was written by day and signed by day;
or written at night and signed at night;
or written at night and signed by day, it is valid.
phrases.notes: The night belongs to the day that follows it, so all of these cases stay on one date.

phrases.english: If written by day and signed at night, it is invalid;
Rabbi Shimon declares it valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נִכְתַּב בַּיּוֹם וְנֶחְתַּם בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט is valid only if it is written and signed on the same calendar date (which starts at night). Written by day and signed that night is פסול, but רבי שמעון rules it כשר.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's general rule: money documents are invalid, but a גט is an exception
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains רבי שמעון. Documents written by day and signed at night are invalid, except a woman's גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון used to say: any document written by day and signed at night is invalid, except for women's bills of divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up רבי שמעון's ruling by quoting his general rule. He makes an exception for a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For most documents, a date earlier than the real signing is dangerous, because it could be used to collect money from too early a date. A גט is not used to collect money, so רבי שמעון is not worried about its date being one day early. A גט still counts as a document like any other; it is simply an exception to this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: legal documents of any kind

phrases.english: For Rabbi Shimon would say:
All documents that were written by day
phrases.notes: Here גיטין means any legal document, not only divorce papers. That is why the last line has to say 'women's' גיטין.

phrases.english: and signed at night are invalid;
except for women's bills of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי שמעון's lenient ruling in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Documents written by day and signed at night are פסול, except a woman's גט.
steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים require a גט to be written and signed on the same date. רבי שמעון does not, because a גט is not a money document.

steps.title: Why did the חכמים require a date on a גט?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule that a גט must be dated.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: For what reason did the חכמים institute writing a date in bills of divorce?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why a גט needs a date at all. It is setting up a disagreement between two אמוראים, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה, especially רבי שמעון, has just said a גט is not about collecting money. So why should its date matter? The next two steps give two different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) instituted, as a rabbinic enactment

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
For what reason did they institute
a date in bills of divorce?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: מִפְּנֵי מָה תִּיקְּנוּ זְמַן בְּגִיטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה by asking for the reason a גט is dated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the rabbinic requirement to write a date in a גט.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Because of his niece
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the date was required because of a man married to his sister's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: because of his sister's daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first answer. The date protects against a husband covering up his wife's sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who loves his wife, for example his niece, might try to save her if she sinned. He could claim he had already divorced her before the sin. A date on the גט shows exactly when the divorce happened, so he cannot make that false claim.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
Because of his sister's daughter.
phrases.notes: He might want to protect a wife he loves from punishment by claiming he divorced her earlier. The date stops that claim.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם בַּת אֲחוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The date prevents a husband from falsely backdating the divorce to protect a wife who sinned.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Because of the produce
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the date was required because of the produce of the wife's fields.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: because of produce.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a second answer that is about money. The date protects the wife's rights to the produce of her fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the marriage, the husband may eat the produce of his wife's fields. That right ends at the divorce. Without a date, he could claim that produce he used after the divorce was taken before it. So ריש לקיש's reason is about money, while רבי יוחנן's reason is about איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce (here: crops from the wife's fields that the husband may eat during the marriage)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for the date in a גט. According to רבי יוחנן, it stops a husband from backdating the divorce to protect a wife who sinned. According to ריש לקיש, it fixes when the husband's right to the produce of her fields ended.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says:
Because of produce.
phrases.notes: The husband may eat the produce of his wife's fields until the divorce. The date shows when that right ended.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, competing answer to the same question that רבי יוחנן answered.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The date marks when the husband's right to the produce of the wife's fields ended, so he cannot claim produce he took after the divorce.

steps.title: Why didn't ריש לקיש agree with רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what pushed ריש לקיש to give a different reason for the date in a גט instead of accepting רבי יוחנן's reason. It then begins the answer with 'אמר לך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש: what is his reason for not saying like רבי יוחנן? He could say to you:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש needed his own reason for dating a גט instead of using רבי יוחנן's. The words 'אמר לך' are setting up the answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two אמוראים give different reasons for one rule, the גמרא often checks whether each one has a problem with the other's reason. Here it starts with ריש לקיש and assumes he must see a weakness in the sister's-daughter explanation. The answer will explain what he thinks that weakness is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? The standard way of asking for someone's logic.
Did not say like (someone): did not take the same position as another sage.
He could say to you. It introduces how a sage would defend his view.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on ריש לקיש's view. The גמרא is only asking why he chose a different reason, and it answers on his behalf right away.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish: what is the reason
that he did not say like Rabbi Yoḥanan?
phrases.notes: He means: why not explain the date because of the man married to his sister's daughter, like רבי יוחנן did?

phrases.english: He could say to you:
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא begins answering for ריש לקיש. His actual words come on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing both reasons in steps 18-19, the גמרא asks why ריש לקיש rejected רבי יוחנן's reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What problem does ריש לקיש see in רבי יוחנן's sister's-daughter reason that made him give a different reason?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer begins with 'אמר לך' and continues on the next amud.
